# Actual-source test of the localized first correction

2026-10-28 HST, E003/S169. Ordinary argument and numerical contract before
execution. The preceding planning turn was NO PROGRESS. Preserve d86adb2,
P32, the closed audit, physical norms and the full stable-wormhole goal.
This test concerns the ACTUAL scalar source, not a uniform arbitrary-source
counterexample. A failure rejects this one-dimensional correction range,
not the coupled inverse or the construction.

## Complete source, domain and proposed correction

Use E_t with e_t=ell_t/N and N=|W_action| beta, and the accepted scalar
trial y_hat of 5967b97. The desired first equation is

    e_t(x,v)=g_hat(v)=b(y_hat,v)/N, v in E_t.

The first inverse is ell_t^-1. Keep the paired first-order mass/log
realization, complementary adjoint and composed squares, original clock,
temperature, scale, full angular/thermal sums, common regulator, contacts,
cutoff transitions and regular disk bolt. No neighborhood or independent
boundary-phase estimate is inferred. E_s admissibility of y_hat, including
its s^2 log(s) bolt term and C2 physical cutoff, is already established.
The complete mixed adjoint makes g_hat an E_t* functional.

Let psi be the unchanged actual localized trial of 85e4598. Test EVERY
correction x_hat=c psi, including its exact first Ritz coefficient and
arbitrary coefficient/application errors whose outputs stay in that range.
The residual is g_hat-e_t(c psi,.), over ALL E_t. We will enclose two
signed evaluations of this complete residual to obtain a lower bound,
not infer an upper certificate from finitely many tests.

## Explicit admissible tests and the first domain implication

Set x=(L-z)/gamma and take b=1,4. Define chi_b(x)=(1-x/b)^8 on [0,b],
zero beyond b, and J_b=z^5 chi_b(x)/gamma. With q(x)=Q(L-gamma*x)/gamma^2,

    I_b(x)=int_x^b [(L-gamma*t)q''(t)+4gamma q'(t)]chi_b(t)dt,
    A_b=-partial_x(z^5 q chi_b),
    xi_b=A_b-z^4 I_b,
    nu_b=xi_b/2+gamma z^4 q chi_b,
    v_b=-3 A_b/2+z^4 I_b.                         (1)

Every expression is an exact polynomial on its support. Use the exact
degree-six finite Q, its exact bolt root and slope, and all finite seed
coefficients. The identity mJ=(zQ''-4Q')chi_b/gamma proves (1) from the
same global York formula as psi. Hence BOTH reconstruction equations hold,
J_b(0)=0 and (Q^2 J_b'/z^4)(L)=0. These fields vanish near the outer end,
have at least six matching zero derivatives at the cutoff, and are
analytic in s at the bolt. They belong to the original form domain by
regular-core approximation; neither an inner wall nor a smooth reflected
surrogate is introduced. The cutoff transition is retained in every
derivative. For these tests b*gamma<1e-12, so y_hat equals its exact y0
profile throughout the support. Its original cutoff remains elsewhere.

## Complete energy comparisons for the test functionals

For a returned field (nu,v) define

 J=sum_{f=nu,v} [||f/z^2||_2^2+||sqrt(Q) f'/z^2||_2^2
                                      +||Delta f/z||_2^2].             (2)

The norms use ORIGINAL dz. This is a deliberately generous, finite
upper estimator on these explicit fields, not a new physical norm. In
the exact local generator of current-finite-local-action-assembly.md use
Q<=.17, |Q'|<10, |Q''|<30, beta>.16 and |log z|<=1/z. The derivative
guards follow directly from the finite coefficient sums. Then
|z^2 D0|<100, |z^2 M0|<11, |z^2 N0|<1 and
||d_i||_2<=13 sqrt(J). Cauchy--Schwarz in each displayed second variation
bounds the normalized Einstein, magnetic and R2 rows respectively by
10000 J, 1000 J and 1e6 J. The coefficient guards used here are
1/C<1, lambda0 B^2/C<1, Z/C<1, 8pi c_R C/B^2<1 and their lower-C
versions. The Weyl polynomial has fewer than 200 product-rule summands;
each has normalized coefficient <1e5 and weighted product at most J.
Its |log z| terms use Delta f/z and f/z^2, so no unweighted logarithm
is dropped. Its bound is 2e7 J. The complete a0, a2 and LLL local
restorations together cost <1e5 J using |c0|<1, |F_eff|<100 and
C/(480pi B^2)<.01. Thus 1e8 J bounds the entire known local energy
with considerable slack, preserving signs only until this upper comparison.

The exact logarithmic geodesic form is retained via the already proved
full-angular bound in current-quartic-ritz-rank-test.md:

 e_geo <= 2 S2/(525pi B^2 beta) int Q[5 A^2/8+3AD/2+D^2]dz,
 A=Q v''', D=3Q'v''/2+Q''v'/2, S2<4C^2/q_ang.           (3)

The test fields and psi are in Dom(X^3) on the actual even double: their
outer data vanish to order at least four, and their cutoffs have more than
three matching derivatives. The metric is the accepted C2,1 metric, not
a smooth replacement. For psi, the accepted covariant third-jet norm
bounds the integral in (3) by twice its square. For the compact tests
compute it directly in x, retaining dz=gamma dx. The accepted complete
reference comparison then gives

 E_upper^2=(1+epsilon)/(1-.0022) [1e8 J+e_geo].          (4)

Use epsilon<=1e-70, a conservative enlargement of the accepted transport
error. Equations (2)-(4), not an unknown graph/physical constant, bound
the energy norm needed for the residual lower test. They imply no C5
admission bound. For psi the z^4 factor is divided algebraically before
exact Laurent/log integration. No artificial radius normalization gain.

## Signed source and complete response evaluations

Let At be the exact positive amplitude of the accepted scalar input.
Use the actual y0/At Legendre combination, not independent modes of the
quantum field. Its complete mixed row yields

 G_i=g_hat(xi_i)/(At gamma)
    =4/beta int_0^b (y0/At) z^-4
                   [Cv tau_bar xi_i-d Delta_bar(tau_bar xi_i)]dx + error.

The entire mixed remainder is bounded by

 |error|<=Kb_rem ||y_hat||Es ||xi_i||Hmu/(beta At gamma),
 ||y_hat||Es<=Ks ||t_hat||Hmu+rho_s.                    (5)

All constants are already established in the scalar-source receipt.
This retains anomaly, density, gauge and finite-return contacts; the
canonical determinant has zero mixed row only in this proved fixed chart.
Use Delta_bar f=z^2[q f_xx+(q_x+2gamma q/z)f_x]. Integration by parts
is justified by the form-domain argument above, including the bolt limit.

For D_i=e_t(psi,xi_i)/gamma evaluate the full local affine action bilinear,
the canonical a2 and LLL rows, and the exact positive-time contact
reallocation using its established coefficient balls. Keep the shared
vacuum coefficient c0 in its original known enclosure. The entire
remaining quantum uncertainty is bounded by

 |D_i-D_local,i| <= [tau_short E_lower,psi E_upper,i
                         +k_plus E_upper,psi E_upper,i]/gamma.        (6)

Here tau_short is the d86adb2 reported bound, which was computed by
dividing its ABSOLUTE column upper bound by E_lower,psi. Consequently
their product is a valid absolute column bound, not an illicit use of
a norm lower bound as an upper bound. The raw positive-time operator
uses k_plus. Its contact coefficient intervals are evaluated directly,
so the separately reported rounded-contact error is not counted twice.
All angular/thermal tails, boundary and bolt returns in (6) remain.
Also charge the accepted retained transport difference, enlarged to
1e-70 E_upper,psi E_upper,i/gamma, so the distinction between the complete
form and its retained transport version cannot disappear in this test.

The local canonical energy has sign minus the I/W Hessian divided by beta.
Its a0 enclosure is charged as |c0| int |vpsi vi|/beta. The a2 and LLL
signs follow the original restoration. Add the positive-time reallocation
a0 int vpsi vi+a2 H4 with the signs recorded in that result.

## Certified numerical contract and full-space consequence

Use outward Arb intervals, fixed correlated parameter receipts and full
cell enclosures for the local response and test energy. Integrate entire
cells, not point samples. The signed source can instead be integrated
exactly. Its factor multiplying y0 is a polynomial f: writing
tau_bar xi=z^8 f0, the divided Laplacian is

 z^-4 Delta_bar(z^8 f0)=z^4{q[40gamma^2 f0-14gamma z f0'+z^2 f0'']
                                      +q'[ -8gamma z f0+z^2 f0']}.

For h=2x+a*x^2 and lambda_k=a*k*(k+1), solve the finite polynomial
identity (partial_x h partial_x-lambda_k)p=f by descending coefficients.
Its diagonal entries a*n*(n+1)-lambda_k are checked nonzero. The
Legendre equation and its actual logarithmic endpoint then give exactly

 int_0^b f(x) Q_k(1+a*x) dx
   =Q_k(1+a*b)h(b)p'(b)-p(b)k[(1+a*b)Q_k-Q_(k-1)]-p(0).

The derivative recurrence is the standard real-Q version of
[DLMF 14.10](https://dlmf.nist.gov/14.10), and the endpoint is
[14.8.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/14.8.E9) with the retained standard-Q
normalization. All degrees used are positive and b>0. The almost-integer
ell coefficient is enclosed by a small ball containing zero; avoid its
ill-conditioned polynomial solve and charge its ENTIRE integral using
Q_ell<=Q_0 and the exact integral of Q_0 on [0,b]. No scalar profile is
discarded. The other three polynomial moment solves use actual degrees,
including nu>7522. These are scalar profiles, not selected quantum modes.
The code checks Q_0(w)=log((w+1)/(w-1))/2 and the polynomial identities.
There is no source quadrature or omitted logarithmic endpoint error.
For k>100, the accepted positive integral gives the complete endpoint
bound Q_k(w)<=Q_0(w)[w+sqrt(w^2-1)]^-k. Use it for BOTH Q_k and Q_(k-1)
in the moment formula; retain their complete interval error. This avoids
a nonfinite large-degree special-function library evaluation without
discarding that profile or its integral. Preserve both development failures.

Let the two complete interval enclosures be G_1,G_2,D_1,D_2 and the
test energy bounds E_1,E_2. If their determinant excludes zero, then
for EVERY c, using the actual field h=D_2 xi_1-D_1 xi_2,

 ||g_hat-e_t(c psi,.)||Et* >=
   At gamma |D_2 G_1-D_1 G_2|/(|D_2|E_1+|D_1|E_2).       (7)

The exact response cancels in h before any norm is taken. The coefficients
in this existence-of-test argument need not be computed exactly; their
complete enclosing intervals prove the lower bound. A finite-dimensional
test suffices for a lower bound on the full dual, not for an upper bound.
Compare (7) with the fixed first-residual screen 1e33. Multiplying by
K_first gives a FLOOR on the corresponding upper-error ESTIMATOR, not a
lower bound on the actual bolt error. Compare that floor also with the
entire 1.667e-9 allowance only to reject an estimator, granting all other
debits zero. No physical margin is assumed available.

If (7) fails the screen, change the correction range, preserve the now
affordable quantum evaluator, and quantify the improvement required. The
complete geodesic-preconditioned first inverse has a nonrestricted leading
range and the already accepted m=12 analytic residual bound; its numerical
applications remain unknown. Compare that specified alternative using
the frozen first-solve receipt, not a newly optimized degree or tail.
If intervals fail to decide (7), report the exact unknown or numerical
loss. Do not present a local matrix or test receipt as a complete residual.

Remaining to-do list: complete actual first correction and residual;
later applications and G_t; all original coupled/admission budgets;

def pa(*ps):
 r=[arb(0)]*max(map(len,ps))

  for i,v in enumerate(p):r[i]+=v

def pm(p,q):

 for i,v in enumerate(p):
  for j,w in enumerate(q):r[i+j]+=v*w
 return r
def pp(p,n):
 r=[arb(1)]
 for _ in range(n):r=pm(r,p)
 return r
def pd(p):return [i*p[i] for i in range(1,len(p))] or [arb(0)]
def pv(p,x):
 r=arb(0)
 for v in reversed(p):r=r*x+v
 return r
def pint(p):return [arb(0)]+[v/(i+1) for i,v in enumerate(p)]
def jets(p,x,n=3):
 r=[]
 for _ in range(n+1):r.append(pv(p,x));p=pd(p)
 return r

class Jet:
 def __init__(self,v=0,i=0,j=0,ij=0):self.v,self.i,self.j,self.ij=map(arb,[v,i,j,ij])
 @staticmethod
 def cast(x):return x if isinstance(x,Jet) else Jet(x)
 def __add__(self,o):
  o=self.cast(o);return Jet(self.v+o.v,self.i+o.i,self.j+o.j,self.ij+o.ij)
 __radd__=__add__
 def __neg__(self):return Jet(-self.v,-self.i,-self.j,-self.ij)
 def __sub__(self,o):return self+-self.cast(o)
 def __rsub__(self,o):return self.cast(o)+-self
 def __mul__(self,o):
  o=self.cast(o)
  return Jet(self.v*o.v,self.i*o.v+self.v*o.i,self.j*o.v+self.v*o.j,
   self.ij*o.v+self.i*o.j+self.j*o.i+self.v*o.ij)
 __rmul__=__mul__
 def __truediv__(self,o):return self*(1/arb(o))
 def __pow__(self,n):
  r=Jet(1)
  for _ in range(n):r=r*self
  return r
def ex(i,j,k):return Jet(1,k*i,k*j,k*k*i*j)

def local_density(p,z,qj,di,dj):
 gamma,C,B2=p['gamma'],p['C'],p['B2']
 q,qx,qxx=qj[:3];ni,ui=di;nj,uj=dj

 M=Jet(gamma*qx/z+gamma**2*q/z**2,delta(ni),delta(nj))
 V=Jet(gamma**2*q/z**2,2*gamma*q*ni[1]/z,2*gamma*q*nj[1]/z,2*q*ni[1]*nj[1])
 D=L-6*M-6*V
 n2,n4=ex(ni[0],nj[0],2),ex(ni[0],nj[0],4)
 u2,um2=ex(ui[0],uj[0],2),ex(ui[0],uj[0],-2)

def qreal(k,w):

  # Q_k(w)<=Q_0(w)*(w+sqrt(w^2-1))^-k for k>=0, w>1.

 v=acb(w).legendre_q(k,type=3)
 assert v.is_finite() and v.imag.contains(0),(k,w,v)

def qmoment(f,k,a,b):
 lam=a*k*(k+1);out=[arb(0)]*len(f)
 for n in range(len(f)-1,-1,-1):

  rem=(a*n*(n+1)-lam)*out[n]+(2*(n+1)**2*out[n+1] if n+1<len(f) else 0)-f[n]
  assert rem.contains(0)
 w=1+a*b;q=qreal(k,w);flux=k*(w*q-qreal(k-1,w))
 return q*(2*b+a*b*b)*pv(pd(out),b)-pv(out,b)*flux-out[0]
